subject: Compute bridge capacity check for SchmidtLabs late-stage commitment
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-10T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: SchmidtLabs — compute bridge estimate + ask for soft-hold

Team,

Late-stage signal from SchmidtLabs — they told Alex today they'll move to signature by EOM if we can guarantee baseline dedicated capacity during Q1 onboarding. High-level ask: they need sustained inference capacity roughly equivalent to 60 A100-40GB slots with bursts to ~90 for the first 6 weeks of production (rush ramp). They prefer H100s if available but A100-equivalent is acceptable with latency SLOs (p95 < 120ms) and prefix cache priming.

Can ops/sales-ops produce an availability snapshot and propose a "soft-hold" window (2–3 months) we can apply while procurement finalizes? Please include:
- Current free capacity by region (us-east, us-west) and by accelerator type (A100/H100)
- Any upcoming maintenance/retirement events in Nov–Jan that could affect this pool
- Suggestions for autoscale fallback (mixed-quantized variants) and estimated cost delta

I attached the SchmidtLabs SOW draft and their capacity ask (schmidtlabs_mop_v3.pdf). We should move quickly — sales indicates they may request a short exclusivity window if we can show runway.

Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: schmidtlabs_mop_v3.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-11T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SchmidtLabs — compute bridge estimate + ask for soft-hold

Connor —

Thanks for the heads-up. Quick inventory snapshot (attached capacity_snapshot_20281110.csv):
- us-west: 48 A100-40GB slots free, 12 H100 slots free (nominal)
- us-east: 38 A100-40GB slots free, 6 H100 slots free
- Scheduled maintenance: 2028-12-12 -> 2028-12-14 (us-west cluster upgrade) — could reduce effective pool by ~10 slots for 48 hours

Notes and recommendations:
1) To meet their sustained 60 A100 requirement we should propose a hybrid plan: reserve 50 A100 slots across us-west + us-east as a soft-hold, and commit autoscale fallback to quantized A100 variants (+~12% model perf delta) for bursts. That gets us to ~80 burst capacity.
2) If they insist on H100s for the initial SLA, we can map 1 H100 -> 2x A100-equivalent for throughput in our runtime (with some latency variance). We only have a total of 18 H100s available across both regions; recommend holding 8 H100s for them if contract requires.
3) Soft-hold policy: mark requested slots as "provisional-commit" in the scheduling layer for 21 days. This keeps autoscaler from reassigning them but allows reclamation with 72-hour notice for critical infra events.

Cost delta estimate (ballpark): +18% unit cost if we reserve H100 subset; +6–9% if we stick to A100s and rely on quantized fallback. Will prep a short one-pager for procurement.

Attaching inventory snapshot.

Ben
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_snapshot_20281110.csv

From: Alex Schmidt <alex.schmidt@schmidtlabs.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@schmidtlabs.com
Date: 2028-11-13T10:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Compute commitment — quick clarification

Connor —

Appreciate the rapid response. A couple clarifications from our side:
- We need the 60 A100 baseline to guarantee our internal SLA to customers; H100s are preferred but not required as long as latency targets are met.
- The ramp profile is aggressive: 2x traffic increase week-over-week for the first 4 weeks. We won't be comfortable if you only offer reclaimed capacity that could be preempted.
- Procurement: we'll need a short exclusivity clause on reserved capacity during the 21-day signature window. We can commit to a 12-month contract at the numbers discussed if you can provide that exclusivity.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support an exclusivity-style soft-hold (non-preemptible for the hold window) and what the cancellation/reclamation terms would be if an emergency capacity event occurs?

Alex Schmidt
VP Product
SchmidtLabs

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-17T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Compute bridge capacity check for SchmidtLabs late-stage commitment

Team —

Following Alex's note, confirm we will:
- Place a 21-day provisional lock on 50 A100 slots and 8 H100 slots across us-west and us-east (split to reduce regional risk). This will be marked as "non-preemptible for hold window" in the contract addendum but with a one-time emergency reclaim clause (48-hour notice) for platform safety events.
- Publish a short runbook for the customer and CS: expected priming time, typical cache warm-up, and the autoscale fallback path (quantized A100 variant) with expected p95 latency deltas.
- Update deal record DEAL-2028-742 in HubSpot with the provisional hold and link DocuSign envelope.

Ben / Marissa — please implement the provisional lock and send me the contract addendum language (I drafted a clause in the attached docuSign stub). Karthik, flag any infra risks (maintenance, retirements) and confirm the 48-hour reclaim window is operationally feasible.

Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
